title: Rule of Five: An Owning Text Class
statement:
A class that owns a raw heap buffer needs **five** special members, not
none: a destructor, a copy constructor, a copy assignment, a move
constructor and a move assignment. Leave any out and the compiler writes a
*member-wise* version that copies the pointer, not the buffer.

## The class

```
class Text
{
public:
    Text(const char* s);               // copies s
    Text(const Text& other);
    Text(Text&& other) noexcept;
    Text& operator=(const Text& other);
    Text& operator=(Text&& other) noexcept;
    ~Text();

    const char* c_str() const;         // never nullptr
    std::size_t size() const;
    void set_char(std::size_t i, char c);   // i < size()

private:
    char* data_;
    std::size_t size_;
};
```

The class is declared in the harness; the constructors, destructor,
assignment operators, `c_str`, `size` and `set_char` are **yours to
define** in your solution. `data_` (or `nullptr`) and `size_` are the only
state.

## Required behaviour

- **Copies are independent:** after `Text b(a);` or `b = a;`, `set_char` on
  one never shows through the other.
- **Self-assignment is safe:** `a = a;` leaves `a` unchanged.
- **Moves steal the buffer:** the source is left empty -- `size() == 0` and
  `c_str()` returns a valid empty string (`""`) -- not dangling.
- **Nothing leaks:** assigning over a live `Text` frees what it owned. The
  harness counts live allocations and reports any left over.

## Watch out

- **Copy assignment must guard against `this == &other`** (or copy before
  freeing). Freeing your own buffer first and then copying from it reads
  freed memory.
- **Free the old buffer before overwriting `data_`** in both assignments,
  or it leaks.
- **A moved-from object is still destroyed.** Set its pointer to
  `nullptr` (and size to 0) so its destructor does not free the buffer the
  new owner now holds -- a double free.
- **`c_str()` must never return `nullptr`;** return `""` when `data_` is
  null.

tests.name: an ordinary word
tests.expected_stdout:
a=[hello] size=5
b=[#ello] size=5
a=[hello] size=5
c=[@ello] size=5
a=[hello] size=5
d=[hello] size=5
a=[] size=0
e=[hello] size=5
d=[] size=0
live=0
tests.description: Copies stay independent; moved-from sources read as empty; live=0.
